wmc_usher.text: Welcome to the Wales Millennium Centre. It opened in 2004 and it is the home of Welsh National Opera.
Look up at the front. The huge poem is by Gwyneth Lewis. In English it reads: In these stones horizons sing.
The Welsh line is Creu gwir fel gwydr o ffwrnais awen. The building is wrapped in Welsh slate in many shades, from several different quarries.

wmc_harpist.text: The acoustics here are famous, so please hush while I tune. It takes me longer than the show.

then.text: Gross, net, tax code. Say it three times, then go and look at your payslip.

else.text: Forty years doing the club's books, and the young ones still don't read their payslips. Come here. Gross is what you're paid. Net, or take-home, is what lands in the bank.
In between come income tax, National Insurance and, if you've a workplace pension, that too.

options: A second tax for no good reason
It builds your state pension record and some benefits

then.text: It feels like it, bach. But no.
Exactly. You need 35 qualifying years for the full new state pension, and NI is how the years get counted.
Ha. If only. The Chancellor can't even claim it on expenses.

else.text: Check the tax code. The usual one is 1257L, which means your first £12,570 a year is tax-free. If yours looks odd, ring HMRC. Wrong codes happen, and they can cost you hundreds. Scotland sets its own income tax bands, mind.
On £2,000 a month with that code, you'd see roughly £190 in tax and £76 in NI. That's before pension.
Auto-enrolment puts most workers aged 22 and over into a pension, and your employer must pay in too, at least 3%. Opting out means turning down part of your pay. Have a slice of bara brith.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
